newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-CAMEROON AND MOROCCO COULD MAKE SIGNIFICANT PROGRESS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CAMEROON AND MOROCCO COULD MAKE SIGNIFICANT PROGRESS.

text.p: Cameroon and Morocco could make a significant step in the direction of a record fourth appearance at the World Cup finals with victories in their African zone qualifying matches this weekend.
Both teams played at the last finals in the United States three years ago and look likely for a repeat appearance with three matches of the qualifying programme still left.
Cameroon host Togo on Sunday while the Morccans travel to Sierra Leone in two of the 10 African qualifying matches scheduled for the weekend.
Cameroon's Indomitable Lions have a chance to go clear at the top of group four where they share the leadership with Angola.
Angola face a difficult trip to Zimbabwe on Sunday while Cameroon are expected to have a far easier encounter against a team they trounced 4-2 away last November.
Under Belgian coach Henri Depireux, Cameroon have again peaked at the right time, rising above federation squabbles and a lack of resources.

Spanish-based goalkeeper Jacques Songo'o says the Belgian has brought discipline and security to the team, who have undergone an almost complete personnel change from the squad who did so badly at the last World Cup.
"The team needs a man with character to lead us and he has got it," said Songo'o.

Morocco also have a foreign coach. Frenchman Henri Michel, ironically in charge of Cameroon at the World Cup in 1994, has seen his side go top of group five despite having played one game fewer than second-placed Sierra Leone and pre-tournament favourites Ghana.
Morocco's last match aaway against Gabon in Libreville three weeks ago was abandoned after 50 minutes after a crowd riot with the north Africans leading 4-0.

FIFA are expected to rule on the outcome of the game next Tuesday. Should Morocco win against Sierra Leone on Sunday and then be awarded the points against Gabon, they will almost certainly be through to France next year.
Ghana host Gabon in Kumasi in the group's other match but, after three successive draws, might have left their challenge too late.
New coach Rinus Israel has dropped striker Tony Yeboah and Bayern Munich defender Samuel Osei Kuffour from his squad for the game.
Nigeria and Tunisia also have golden opportunities to stretch their group leadership at the weekend.
Tunisia play Liberia at home in Tunis on Sunday in group two while Nigeria are away to Burkina Faso in Ouagadougou the same day.

The Nigerians lead the standings in group one despite some unimpressive performances. It will be the second game in charge for Frenchman Philippe Troussier, who has warned his charges of taking the qualifiers for granted.
"Nigeria's Dream Team was fantastic in winning the Olympic gold medal last year but this is the World Cup qualifiers now, and it is a completely different challenge," Troussier said.
The Super Eagles travel to Burkina without suspended defender Austin Eguavoen and Taribo West and have recalled Uche Okafor from American club Kansas City Wiz.
Group three presents possibly the best potential for drama this weekend with leaders Congo away to Zambia and Zaire playing South Africa in neutral Togo.

Congo are emerged as surprise leaders but are not fancied against Zambia, who have captain Kalusha Bwalya back for their match in Lusaka on Sunday, and looked devastating in beating Malawi 4-0 in a warm-up game last Saturday.
That will give South Africa a chance to go back into a share of the group's leadership if they beat Zaire in Lome on Sunday.
The match has been switched from Kinshasa because of the civil war in Zaire.
